title: Smoky Chicken Bowls
seoTitle: Mediterranean Chicken Farro Bowls | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Herb chicken with farro, cucumber, and hummus for ten
subtitle: Herb chicken with farro, cucumber, and hummus for ten
description: Lemon-oregano chicken roasts and slices over chewy farro with cucumber, tomato, olives, and hummus. A bright, filling bowl that breaks up heavy comfort-food rotations.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Smoky Chicken Bowls in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Cook the farro
steps.instruction: Simmer farro in salted water 25–30 minutes until chewy-tender. Drain and toss with 2 tablespoons olive oil. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Roast the chicken
steps.instruction: Coat chicken with lemon juice, oregano, salt, pepper, and 2 tablespoons olive oil. Roast at 425°F 22–25 minutes until internal temp reaches 165°F. Slice. Target oven/smoker temperature: 425°F.

steps.title: Prep the vegetables
steps.instruction: Combine cucumber, tomatoes, and olives. Dress lightly with remaining olive oil and lemon juice. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build the bowl line
steps.instruction: Set out farro, sliced chicken, vegetable mix, hummus, and feta in labeled containers. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Assemble and serve
steps.instruction: Portion farro into bowls, top with chicken, vegetables, dollop of hummus, and crumbled feta. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

proTips: Pearl farro cooks faster than whole—check package time and adjust.
Pickled red onions add punch without extra prep mid-service.
Grilled zucchini strips use the same oven time as chicken.
tonightSpread: Bowls with warm pita wedges and extra lemon wedges.
Simple tabbouleh on the side if you want more veg volume cheaply.
leftovers: Stuff into pita with extra hummus for quick lunches.
Farro and veg mix makes a cold grain salad the next day.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Farro is nutty, filling, and different from the usual rice line-up. Mediterranean flavors feel light but the portions are hall-sized, not spa-sized.
mealPrepNotes: Cook farro ahead—it holds well. Dice vegetables uniform. Chicken can roast while farro simmers to save time.
